note: Patterns that map the compiler's first error to a class of the model's CheckError, tried in order. A failed instantiation's first error carries the note of the constraint that failed. 'has no attribute 'copy'' comes before unknownAttribute: the compiler reports .copy() of a value that is not Copyable as a missing attribute, the model as notCopyable. 'has no attribute' is the compiler's error for an unknown field and for an unknown method alike, on any type. 'does not designate a value with an origin', the compiler's error for moving an element out of a list or an array, or a value out through a 'ref' binding, comes before escapingReference, whose pattern also matches 'origin'. 'use of invalidated interior reference' is the compiler's error for a reference to a list element used after the list changed. 'is uninitialized at (the implicit )?return from this function', the compiler's error for a 'mut' parameter or the 'self' of '__init__' left partly uninitialized when the function returns, comes before uninitializedUse, whose pattern also matches 'uninitialized'. 'invalid use of mutating method on rvalue' is the compiler's error for a 'mut self' method called on a value that cannot be changed, such as 'p^' or a 'read' parameter, and 'value passed to mutable argument ... must be mutable' its error for such a value passed to a 'mut' parameter; the model reports both as immutablePlace. In the subset, a field has a non-'Deinitable' type when it lies on a cycle of structs made only of list and array edges, as in a struct that holds a list or an array of itself; the compiler also reports it for a cycle with a list edge and a by-value edge whose by-value holder is `@fieldwise_init` and declared first, a compiler bug (D-0004). 'attempt to resolve a recursive reference to declaration' is the compiler's error for a struct that holds itself by value, directly or through other structs. 'does not conform to trait 'Writable'' is the compiler's error for printing a value that print cannot write. 'aliasing values passed immutably' is the compiler's error for a location passed immutably that a 'mut' argument of the same call aliases, such as a returned reference and the place it points into; 'immutable' does not match 'immutably'. 'value passed to mutable argument ... must be mutable' is also the compiler's error for a 'mut' argument that is a call returning an immutable reference, and for a temporary passed 'mut', which the model reports as notAPlace (#81). 'no matching function in initialization' is the compiler's error for every initialization whose arguments fit no initializer: a construction with wrong arguments, a literal that does not fit the list or array it initializes, and List[T](...) with arguments or from a source that is not a list or an array of T. 'cannot construct 'T' with itself, you can remove the constructor call' is its error for the same misfit when the one argument has the type T itself, such as List[T](xs) from a List[T] whose elements cannot be copied (#103). Both are matched whole, so that no other message reaches noMatchingInit, and the second comes first, since it holds a type name that a later pattern, such as 'immutable', could match. 'used with all fields manually initialized but without calling an '__init__' method' is the compiler's error for a struct built field by field and then used whole, which the model reports as uninitializedUse, as the compiler does for a part of one (#51).
